theory.overview: A heap is a specialized tree-based data structure that satisfies the heap property: in a max heap, any node is greater than or equal to its children; in a min heap, any node is less than or equal to its children. Heaps are commonly implemented as binary trees using arrays. They provide O(log n) insertion and extraction of the max/min element, making them ideal for priority queues, heap sort, and finding kth largest/smallest elements.

keyConcepts.name: Heap Property
keyConcepts.description: Max Heap: parent ≥ children. Min Heap: parent ≤ children. The root is always the max (or min) element.

keyConcepts.name: Array Implementation
keyConcepts.description: Heaps are typically stored in arrays. For 0-indexed: parent(i) = (i-1)/2, left(i) = 2i+1, right(i) = 2i+2.

keyConcepts.name: Heapify Up/Down
keyConcepts.description: Heapify Up (bubble up): for insertions. Heapify Down (sift down): for extractions. Both O(log n).

keyConcepts.name: Priority Queue
keyConcepts.description: Abstract data type implemented efficiently with heaps. Supports: insert, extract-max/min, peek.

algorithmSteps.description: Insert 3: Add to end. 3 < 5, heap property maintained.
Insert 8: Add to end. 8 > 5, bubble up! Swap with parent.
8 is now root. No more parents to compare.
Insert 1: Add to end. 1 < 3, no bubble needed.
Insert 7: Add to end. 7 > 3, bubble up! Swap with parent.
Extract max: Remove root (8), replace with last element (1).
Sift down: 1 < 7 and 5, swap with max child (7).

minigame.title: Heap Operations Visualizer
minigame.description: Insert and extract elements from a heap. Watch bubble up and sift down operations maintain heap property.
instructions: Insert values to see bubble up (heapify up)
Extract max to see sift down (heapify down)
Observe how heap property is maintained
